questions.text: What documentation must architects maintain for government contracts to comply with RA 9184 and COA audit requirements?

options.text: Only final invoices, which is insufficient for comprehensive compliance with audit standards.
Complete records of work performed, invoices, supporting documents, and correspondence
Only photographs of the project, which do not fulfill the detailed documentation requirements.
No records are required, which is incorrect as thorough documentation is mandated by law.

rationale.a: Final invoices alone lack supporting documentation for audit verification.
rationale.c: Photos are supplementary; comprehensive administrative records are required.
rationale.d: Documentation is mandatory under RA 9184 and COA audit requirements.
rationale.correct: RA 9184 and COA audits require complete documentation: work records, invoices, supporting documents, and correspondence demonstrating compliance and justifying decisions.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184 requires complete project documentation including work records, invoices, documents, and correspondence for COA audit.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of RA 9184 & 2016 Revised IRR (Updated 2024)?

options.text: To regulate architectural education, ensuring that all educational institutions comply with national standards
To establish the legal framework for government procurement of goods, services, and infrastructure
To license private architects, providing them with the necessary credentials to practice
To abolish government agencies that are deemed redundant or inefficient

rationale.a: Confuses RA 9184 with education regulation (addressed separately under RA 9266 for architectural licensing).
rationale.c: RA 9184 regulates government procurement, not architect licensing (RA 9266 governs licensing).
rationale.d: RA 9184 does not address agency dissolution; it establishes procurement procedures.
rationale.correct: RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act) establishes the legal framework for all government procurement of goods, services, and infrastructure projects.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184 is the Government Procurement Reform Act governing all government procurement of goods, services, and infrastructure.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three procurement methods under RA 9184?

options.text: Competitive bidding
Limited bidding
Single source procurement
Negotiated settlement

rationale.a: Competitive bidding is the standard, first method under RA 9184.
rationale.b: Limited bidding applies when only few qualified firms exist.
rationale.c: Single source procurement is used in exceptional cases (emergency, sole expertise, existing agreements).
rationale.d: Negotiated settlement is a non-statutory concept not authorized by RA 9184.
rationale.correct: RA 9184's primary method is public competitive bidding (Sec 10); alternatives include limited source bidding (Sec 49), direct contracting (Sec 50), and repeat order (Sec 51); 'negotiated settlement' is not a recognized mode.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184's three procurement methods are competitive bidding, limited bidding, and single source procurement.

questions.text: What are the two core governing principles mandated by RA 9184 that directly affect architectural procurement?

options.text: Cost and quality only, which overlooks the importance of transparency and competitiveness
Transparency and competitiveness
Speed and affordability, which are not the primary focus of RA 9184
Innovation and sustainability, which are encouraged but not the core principles

rationale.a: Cost and quality are considerations within the transparency/competitiveness framework, not the core governing principles.
rationale.c: Speed and affordability are objectives, not the foundational governing principles.
rationale.d: Innovation and sustainability are important but not identified as the core principles.
rationale.correct: RA 9184 mandates transparency (openness and accountability) and competitiveness (equal opportunity for qualified consultants) as core governing principles.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184's core principles are transparency (open processes) and competitiveness (equal opportunity for all qualified architects).

questions.text: What is the source-safe framing of RA 12009 (signed 20 July 2024) relative to RA 9184, and what should architects do?

options.text: RA 12009 is a new Implementing Rules and Regulations updating RA 9184; architects only need to re-read the old IRR
RA 12009 is a new statute (New Government Procurement Act) that revises RA 9184; architects should track the new law, its IRR, and PhilGEPS e-procurement requirements
RA 12009 repeals all procurement rules so architects no longer need to bid for government work
RA 12009 only applies to private architectural projects, so government architects can ignore it

rationale.a: RA 12009 is not an IRR; it is a new statute that revises RA 9184 itself.
rationale.b: RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act of 2024, signed 20 July 2024) is a successor statute that revises RA 9184. Architects should follow the new law, its IRR, and the PhilGEPS e-procurement system.
rationale.c: RA 12009 revises rather than abolishes government procurement; bidding rules remain, modernized.
rationale.d: RA 12009 applies to government procurement, not private projects; government-side architects must follow it.
rationale.correct: RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act of 2024, signed 20 July 2024) is a successor statute that revises RA 9184. Architects should follow the new law, its IRR, and the PhilGEPS e-procurement system.
rationale.takeaway: Do not conflate a statute with an IRR. RA 12009 is the new law; its IRR is a separate instrument. Track both plus PhilGEPS for e-procurement.

questions.text: Which government entity oversees the evaluation and selection of architects in RA 9184 procurement?

options.text: Board of Architecture, which is responsible for setting professional standards and ensuring compliance with architectural laws
Bids and Awards Committee (BAC)
Commission on Audit, tasked with ensuring transparency and accountability in government procurement processes
Department of Budget and Management, which oversees the allocation of funds and ensures fiscal responsibility in public projects

rationale.a: The Board of Architecture regulates the profession, not procurement selection.
rationale.c: COA audits completed projects; it does not evaluate and select consultants.
rationale.d: DBM handles budgets; the BAC conducts selection and evaluation.
rationale.correct: The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) evaluates qualifications, shortlists firms, and selects architects for government procurement projects.
rationale.takeaway: The Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) evaluates and selects architects for government procurement under RA 9184.

questions.text: Under RA 9184, can an architect be hired by a government client based solely on personal connection or informal arrangement?

options.text: Yes, if the client prefers, although this may lead to questions of transparency and fairness
Yes, for small projects only, provided the total cost does not exceed a specified threshold
No; selection must follow formal competitive procurement procedures
Only if the fee is very low, which might compromise the quality of work delivered

rationale.a: Client preference cannot override statutory procurement procedures.
rationale.b: No project size exempts from formal procurement; the competitiveness principle applies universally.
rationale.d: Fee level does not justify informal procurement; transparency and competitiveness apply regardless of contract value.
rationale.correct: RA 9184 mandates formal competitive procurement procedures; personal relationships and informal arrangements are prohibited regardless of project size or fee.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184 prohibits informal selection; all government architectural procurement requires formal competitive procedures.

questions.text: How must scope changes be handled in a RA 9184 government contract?

options.text: The architect can perform additional work without notifying the client, which is against RA 9184 regulations
Changes require formal change orders signed by both parties, documenting reason, work description, and fee/time impact
Only the client can initiate changes, which limits collaborative flexibility
Changes are prohibited after contract signing, which is not practical for project evolution

rationale.a: Unilateral work performance without authorization violates the contract and RA 9184.
rationale.c: Either party can propose changes; both must agree via formal change order.
rationale.d: Changes are permitted through formal procedures; absolute prohibition is unrealistic.
rationale.correct: RA 9184 requires formal change orders documenting the change, reason, scope, and fee/schedule impact; both parties must sign.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184 requires formal, signed change orders documenting reason, work scope, and fee/time impacts.

questions.text: What happens if two bidding architectural firms communicate to arrange fees or coordinate their proposals?

options.text: It is acceptable as long as disclosure occurs, provided all parties are informed and agree
It violates RA 9184 and can result in permanent disqualification from government procurement
It is only prohibited if the client finds out, which could lead to penalties if discovered
It has no legal consequences unless it affects the outcome of the bidding process

rationale.a: Disclosure does not legalize collusion; the prohibition is absolute.
rationale.c: Violation occurs when communication occurs, regardless of discovery.
rationale.d: RA 9184 provides severe sanctions for collusion including permanent disqualification.
rationale.correct: RA 9184 strictly prohibits collusion, bid-rigging, and coordination; violators face permanent disqualification from government procurement.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184 strictly prohibits collusion, bid-rigging, and fee coordination; violations result in permanent government procurement disqualification.

questions.text: What must be clearly stated in an architectural consulting contract under RA 9184 to avoid disputes?

options.text: Only the fee amount, which is the primary concern for both parties
Scope of services, deliverables, submission schedules, revision rounds, and compensation structure
Only the project timeline, as it dictates the overall project flow
Only the client's name, which is essential for contract validity

rationale.a: Fee alone is insufficient; comprehensive scope definition is essential.
rationale.c: Timeline is necessary but insufficient without scope clarity.
rationale.d: Client identification is basic but does not address substantive contract terms.
rationale.correct: RA 9184 contracts must clearly define scope of services, deliverables, schedules, revision rounds, and compensation to prevent disputes and protect both parties.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9184 contracts require clear definition of scope, deliverables, schedules, revisions, and fees.
